task.title: Push Commits
task.shortdesc: Send your local commits to the remote repository so others can see them.

info.p: The push goes to the remote the current branch tracks. To push to a different one, use the submenu in the menu or the menu.

result.p: The Git Client sends your commits to the remote branch. If the branch exists only locally, it creates a matching remote branch and starts tracking it. When the repository has more than one remote, you are asked which one to publish the branch to.
result.note: To keep two servers in sync with a single push, give one remote several push URLs with git remote set-url --add --push <remote> <url>. The Git Client pushes by remote name, so one reaches every URL you added. This is one way to mirror a repository, which is a kind of push-to-all-remotes action.
